body_text:
Strong induction. Let $P(n)$ be a predicate on $\mathbb{N}$. If,
for every $n$, the assumption that $P(k)$ holds for all $k<n$
implies $P(n)$, then $P(n)$ holds for all $n$. Strong induction
and ordinary induction are equivalent: ordinary induction can be
applied to the cumulative statement that $P(k)$ holds for every
$k\leq n$.
